senses.gloss:
Tṛṇa, ‘grass,’ is often mentioned in the Rigveda^1 and later.^2
It was used as straw to roof in a house or hut.^3
1) i. 161, 1; 162, 8, 11; x. 102, 10,
etc.
2) Av. ii. 30, 1; vi. 54, 1, etc.;
Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, iii. 22; viii. 24,
etc.
3) Av. iii. 12, 5; ix. 3, 4, 7.

Tṛṇa-jalāyuka, ‘caterpillar,’ is mentioned in the Bṛhad-
āraṇyaka Upaniṣad (iv. 2, 4).

Tṛṇa-skanda occurs once in the Rigveda^1 as the name of
a prince, his subjects (viśaḥ) being referred to.^2 The word
may originally have meant ‘grasshopper.’^3
1) i. 172, 3.
2) Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 159, takes viśaḥ as ‘cantons,’ but see Viś.
3) St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.
